Euskara:eu.1. ¿Qué hace un sacerdote? \n El pr:
1.  Apaiz batek zer egiten du?  
    Apaiz baten helburua da pertsonak Jesusekin eramatea eta Jesus pertsonetara eramatea. Horretarako batez ere Hitzaren predikazioa eta Mezaren Gurutzatua eskaintzen du.
Euskara:eu.Su vida diaria consiste en administrar l: Bere eguneroko bizitza sakramentuak administratzea da —Bataioa, Berretspena, Eukaristia, Penitentzia eta Elkarrekin adiskidetasuna, Gaixoen Ignazioaren Sakramentua eta Auzitegia (Orden Sakratua gotzainak administratzen du)— eta bere komunitateko premia espirituala eta gizatiarra zaintzea.
Euskara:eu.2. ¿Qué es exactamente una “vocación”?:
2.  Zein da zehazki “vocazio” bat?  
    Vocazioa da Jainkoaren dei bat beretzat eta bere Erresumaren alde zerbait jakin bat egiteko. Pertsona guztien vocazio nagusia santua izatea da: Jainkoa maitatzea eta zerbitzatzea, bere aginduak betetzea eta Kristorekin lankidetzan aritzea salbamena lortzeko besteen maitatuz eta zerbitzatuz.
Euskara:eu.Pero todos somos llamados también a una: Baina denok deiak gara baita ere vocazio sekundario batera, bizitza-egoera batean non santuen izan behar dugun.
Euskara:eu.3. ¿Cuáles son esas “vocaciones secunda:
3.  Zein dira vocazio sekundario horiek deitzen naitezkeenak?  
    Jende asko ezkontzara deiatua dago, baina akatsa da automatikoki hori zure vocazioa dela pentsatzea. Apaiztza, bizitza erlijiosoa anai edo arreba bezala edo diakonatua izan zaitezke ere.
Euskara:eu.Finalmente, algunos siguen a Cristo en e: Azkenik, batzuek Kristoaren jarraitzaile izaten jarraitzen dute bizitza solteko egoeran. Gogoratu: normala da ezkontza eta familia desiratzen izatea. Desira horrek ez du baztertzen apaizgoko deia izan dezakezunik.
Euskara:eu.4. ¿Cómo puedo saber a qué me llama Dio:
4.  Nola jakin dezaket Jainkoak zer deitzen nauen?  
    Egunero otoitzean eskatu behar diozu Jainkoari bere plana agerian jartzeko. Ez galdetu: “Zer egin nahi dut heldua naizenean?”, baizik eta: “Jesusek, zuk zer nahi duzu nik egin dezadan?”. Entzun erantzuna!
Euskara:eu.El lugar principal donde Dios habla es e: Jainkoak hitz egiten duen lekurik nagusia bihotza da. Entzun bihotzez. Gainera, apaizgoko deia discernitzea beti egiten da Elizarekin. Tokiko gotzaia, deialdi bulegoaren eta seminarioaren laguntzaz, da azken batean deiaren bermea ematen duena.
Euskara:eu.5. ¿Puedo ser feliz si no sigo el plan:
5.  Zoriontsu izan naiteke Jainkoak niretzat duen plana jarraitu ez badut?  
    Sortu zintuzten deia jarraitu ezean, bizitza honetan nolabaiteko zoriontasuna lortu dezakezu eta salbatua izan daitekezu, baina inoiz ez zara hain beti eta guztiz zoriontsu izango zure benetako deia jarraituko bazenuen bezainbeste.
Euskara:eu.Por eso es tan importante discernir corr: Horregatik da hain garrantzitsua ongi discernitzea. Jakina, deia bakoitzean proba eta zailtasunak daude, baina baita handia ere pozik bizitza Jesusegatik ematean.
Euskara:eu.6. ¿Son felices la mayoría de los sacer:
6.  Apaizen gehienak zoriontsuak al dira bere deian?  
    Apaizen gehienak oso zoriontsuak dira! Apaizbizitza sakonki atsegina da, bai bizitza honetan, bai betikoan.
Euskara:eu.Los medios de comunicación a veces dan u: Hedabideek batzuetan apaizen irudi okerra ematen dute, frustrazionatuta edo zoriontsu ez diruditen moduan aurkeztuz, edo gutxi batzuek sortutako eskandalotara mugatuz. Hori sinpleki ez da egia.
Euskara:eu.7. ¿Por qué los sacerdotes no pueden ca:

Euskara:eu.El celibato es un signo poderoso para el: Solterotasuna munduari adierazpen indartsua da: bakarrik Jesusek eman diezagukeen zoriontasuna eskatzen dugula esaten du. Ezkontzari eta familiari uko egiteak erakusten du Kristoa benetakoa dela eta bere alde bizitza emateko merezi duela.
Euskara:eu.Toda vocación exige sacrificios, pero ha: Deia bakoitzak sakrifizioak eskatzen ditu, baina maitasunagatik sakrifikatzean poz handia dago. Apaiz batek esaten zuenez: “Egia da inork ez didala ‘aita’ esango, baina milaka jendek ‘aita’ deitzen didate”.
Euskara:eu.8. ¿Alguna vez se permitirá que los sac:
8.  Noizbait ahal izango al dute apaizek ezkondu?  
    Solterotasuna beti egongo da Elizan, ez delako arau soil bat bakarrik, karisma bat baizik, opari espirituala eta ugalkortasun iturria. Jesukristoa ere soltekoa izan zen. San Paulo ere bai.
Euskara:eu.El celibato ayuda al sacerdote a unirse: Solterotasunak apaiza Kristorekin elkartuago izaten laguntzen du eta Jainkoaren Erreinuaren seinale izaten da. Eliza katolikoan badaude ezkondutako apaiz batzuk, baina salbuespenak dira.
Euskara:eu.Si alguna vez el Espíritu Santo quisiera: Noizbait Espiritu Santuak aldaketa bat nahi izango balu, Aita Santua eta gotzainek egiteke egingo lukete. Baina seminariora «espetantza» horrekin joatea akats larria litzateke.

    Agian bai, baina gakoa da hori Elizarentzat onena izango ote litzatekeen. Erreinuagatik hartutako solterotasunak lekukotasun indartsua ematen du: Jesukristoa benetakoa dela eta guztiz eskaintzeko merezi duela.
Euskara:eu.Además, las vocaciones sacerdotales han: Gainera, apaiz deiek azken hamarkadetan izugarri hazi dute Afrikan, Asian eta Hego Amerikan, Europa eta Estatu Batuetan jaitsi diren bitartean. Arazoa ez da solterotasuna, baizik eta sakonago dauden faktore kultural eta sozialak.
Euskara:eu.10. ¿Estaré solo si me hago sacerdote?:
10.  Bakarrik egongo naiz apaiz bihurtzen banaiz?  
    Bakardadea deia guztien parte da, baina apaizak tarteka oso gutxi daude bakarrik: bizitzako momentu garrantzitsuenetan laguntzen diete pertsonenei —jaiotza, sakramentuak, ezkontza, heriotza— eta beren komunitatean inguruan bizi dira.
Euskara:eu.Cuando llega la soledad, Jesús llena ese: Bakardadea iristen denean, Jesusek hutsune hori betetzen du, deia guztietan egiten duen bezala.
Euskara:eu.11. ¿Los sacerdotes reciben salario? \:
11.  Apaizek soldata jasotzen al dute?  
    Bai, nahiz eta bizitza xumea izan. Gastuak estaltzeko, ibilgailua mantentzeko, atseden hartzeko eta jarduera normalak egiteko beharrezkoa jasotzen dute. Gainera, parrokiek babesa ematen diete ostatua eta janaria emanez, beraz gastuak minimoak izaten dira.
Euskara:eu.12. ¿Pueden divertirse los sacerdotes?:
12.  Apaizek entretenitu al daitezke?  
    Noski. Apaizek kirolak egin ditzakete, filmak ikusi, irakurri, bidaiatu, antzokira joan, arrantzan ibili, futbolean edo golfan jolastu, beti bizitza kristauarekin bat datorrenean.
Euskara:eu.13. Si me atrae el sacerdocio, ¿signifi:
13.  Apaizgogoa erakartzen badit, deia dudala esan nahi al du?  
    Agian bai, baina ez derrigor. Garrantzitsua da otoitz egitea, Misan parte hartzea, kristau moduan bizitzea eta apaiz edo deialdi zuzendariarekin hitz egitea. Haiek lagundu diezazukete garbi discernitzen.
Euskara:eu.14. No soy muy “santo”. ¿Aun así puedo:
14.  Ez naiz oso «santu». Hala ere apaiza izan naiteke?  
    Bai. Santutasuna bizitza osoko bide bat da. Jainkoak bere apaizak pixkanaka osatzen ditu. Sakramentuaren erabil ezazu, egunero otoitz egin eta ikusiko duzu Kristo nola bihurtzen zaituen.
Euskara:eu.15. ¿Es fácil llegar a ser sacerdote?:
15.  Erraza al da apaiz izatea?  
    Ez. Prestakuntza serioa eskatzen da: lau urteko unibertsitate (filosofia barne) eta beste lau seminarion teologia magisterioa lortzeko. Baina ez gaizki izan: seminarioa esperientzia zoragarria da eta Jainkoak graciarik beharrezkoa ematen du.
Euskara:eu.16. ¿Es necesaria tanta educación? \n:

    Bai. Apaiza ongi prestatua egon behar da gizaki-zientzietan, teologian eta bizitza espiritualean zerbitzatzeko jakintzaz eta fededunekin errespetatua izateko. Arima bakoitza preziatua da eta prestatutako artzain bat merezi du.
Euskara:eu.17. ¿Qué cualidades busca la Iglesia en:

    Praktikatzen den katolikoa izan behar du, egunean otoitz egiten duena, aginduak bizitzen dituena, besteei zerbitzatzen diona, osasun fisiko, mentala eta emozional ona duena, eta gaitasun intelektual ertaina edo altuagoa duena. Batez ere, Jainkoaren borondateari irekita egon behar du.
Euskara:eu.18. Si entro al seminario “para probar”:

English:en.**¿Cómo conocer el plan de Dios para tu:
**How to know God’s plan for your life?**  
Follow these recommendations and God will help you understand what He is calling you to in your life!
English:en.1. **Oración** \n La oración es una:
1.  **Prayer**  
    Prayer is a conversation with God, not just reciting prayers, but speaking to the Lord from the heart. Every day read the Bible and talk to Jesus as if He were your best friend. Ask Him to reveal His plan: “Jesus, I want to want what You want. Here I am, Lord; I come to do Your will.” Trust fully that God has a plan for you.
English:en.2. **Sacramentos** \n El alma es la:
2.  **The Sacraments**  
    The soul is the window through which we can see God and hear His voice. If the window is dirty from sin, it must be cleaned through Confession to be in union with God. When you receive Communion, ask Jesus to show you your vocation.
English:en.3. **Buena información** \n Es impo:
3.  **Good information**  
    It is impossible to discover your vocation without good information. What does it mean to have a Christian and holy marriage? What do priests do? What is the life of a sister or brother in religious life like? Look for reliable information and then bring what you have learned back to prayer.
English:en.4. **La Santísima Virgen** \n María:
4.  **The Blessed Virgin**  
    Mary is the supreme example of openness to God’s will. Are you open to God’s will for you? Pray three Hail Marys each day, specifically to know your vocation and have the courage to follow it.
English:en.5. **Ir de retiro** \n ¡Los milagro:
5.  **Go on a retreat**  
    Miracles happen on retreats! One of the surest ways to discover God’s plan for you is to enter silence and prayer for an extended time. Ask trusted people to help you find a good retreat.
English:en.6. **Pide consejo** \n No trates de:
6.  **Ask for advice**  
    Do not try to discern your vocation alone, without the help of the Church. Talk to a sister, a priest, or a deacon you trust.
English:en.Cuando llegue el momento, ¡debes actuar!: When the time comes, you must act! Move in the direction your heart indicates, with the confidence that God will never send you to a place where His grace cannot sustain you.
English:en.## **Cada vocación es un misterio: cada: ## **Each vocation is a mystery: each person goes through these stages differently.**
English:en.Algunos solo pasarán por las etapas para: Some will only go through the stages to discover the meaning of their lay life and others to find their priestly vocation.
English:en.Si estás en la etapa 1 has experimentado: If you are in stage 1 you have recently experienced a call to give yourself to the Lord. This initial stage of discernment often occurs during childhood, perhaps at Mass, for example from religious, seeing Christians who love God radically, thanks to committed catechists, with your parents, in a Catholic school class or when a priest invites you to consider the priesthood.
English:en.Esta atracción inicial y misteriosa por: This initial and mysterious attraction to give everything to God is mysterious. Becoming a priest, dedicating yourself to religious life, being salt and light among all people… It is even more mysterious because you have almost no information about vocation or discernment.
English:en.Las emociones principales son emoción y: The main emotions are excitement and wonder: “Could God really be calling me to give myself entirely?”
English:en.Piensas en ello de vez en cuando, pero n: You think about it from time to time, but not every day. The idea comes up at Mass, when praying at night or when someone mentions it. But you think: “Surely it’s not for me,” “I don’t need anything else,” “I already go to Mass and pray a little”... “Being a layperson is not a vocation” or “I will marry like everyone else”
English:en.Te das cuenta de que esa llamada no desa: You realize that this call does not go away, even if you try. You give in and stop avoiding it. You begin to pray more, grow in faith and seek help from a spiritual director. Likewise, you find Christ in your brother and in those in need and open yourself to concrete self-giving to others. You begin to fight the spiritual battle of surrendering to God’s will; some days you win the battle and other days you lose. In this stage you discover a different peace, one that is born from deepening your interior life and bringing Christ into every aspect of your life. Here you learn to overcome fears: the fear of missing out, of not being enough or of being labeled a “saint.”
English:en.Igual no encuentras todavía paz y confir: You may still not find peace and confirmation; you discover that your fears are about the priesthood or religious life: celibacy, loneliness, public speaking, being a good priest… you face them and feel the joy of serving God and others. Your desire to serve others grows and you experience happiness while serving.
English:en.Vas avanzando hacia la entrega a la volu: You move forward toward giving yourself to God’s will. After praying, informing yourself and participating in retreats, you feel peace and confirm God’s call to leave everything.
English:en.Tu director espiritual te dice que tiene: Your spiritual director tells you that you have the signs and qualifications. The essential element is understanding that discernment cannot progress further outside the seminary or novitiate; you are simply going in circles.
English:en.Entras al seminario o al noviciado y viv: You enter the seminary or the novitiate and live surrounded by others who are also discerning, and your life revolves around daily prayer, Mass, and serious study of the faith.

English:en.Es el momento de consolidar tu camino es: It is the moment to consolidate your spiritual and vocational path.
English:en.Llevas tiempo en el seminario y has crec: You have been in the seminary for some time and have grown greatly in faith, prayer, and knowledge. You know Jesus personally and are ready to teach and serve. Now the hard work is daily, but you feel that you will surely be a priest and you know you can fulfill that responsibility.
English:en.Si estás a punto de casarte, también pue: If you are about to marry, you can also experience this inner peace that springs from living your vocation with commitment. You know Jesus personally and are ready to love, teach, and serve within your family. The daily work is constant: building a solid home, accompanying your spouse, educating the children, and living the faith together. You feel that God has called you to this mission and you know that, with His help, you can order all social life from within and transform the world through the love and self-giving of your family.
English:en.## Los votos religiosos: pobreza, castid: ## The religious vows: poverty, chastity, and obedience, a path of total love
English:en.**Por amor a Cristo, muchos hombres y mu: **For the love of Christ, many men and women in the Church leave everything.** Not out of contempt for the world, but out of love for the coming Kingdom. In a time marked by the pursuit of pleasure, wealth, and personal autonomy, the religious vows are a **prophetic light** that shows another way of living: that of **Jesus, poor, chaste, and obedient**.
English:en.Un _voto_ es una **promesa hecha a Dios*: A _vow_ is a **promise made to God**. It is not a mere human resolution, but a sacred commitment by which a person gives themselves to the Lord with their whole being. The **Code of Canon Law** defines it as a “free and deliberate promise made to God of a possible and better good” (cf. c. 1191).
English:en.Entre todos los votos, destacan los **vo: Among all vows, the **religious vows** stand out, by which members of institutes of consecrated life solemnly commit to live the _evangelical counsels_: **poverty, chastity, and obedience**. These are not simple renunciations, but **ways of loving more and better**, reproducing in one’s own life the very style of Jesus Christ.
English:en.> “Por medio de los votos de pobreza, ca:
> “By means of the vows of poverty, chastity, and obedience, you can be bearers of light for the women and men of our time.”  
> — _Pope Francis, World Day for Consecrated Life_
English:en.### ✨ El voto de castidad: amar con cora: ### ✨ The vow of chastity: to love with an undivided heart
English:en.El **canon 599** del Derecho Canónico en: Canon 599 of the Code of Canon Law teaches:
English:en.> “El consejo evangélico de castidad asu: > “The evangelical counsel of chastity assumed for the Kingdom of Heaven, as a sign of the future world and source of a more abundant fruitfulness in an undivided heart, entails the obligation to observe perfect continence in celibacy.”
English:en.El voto de castidad no es una simple abs: The vow of chastity is not a mere abstention, but a **way of loving as Christ loved**. Whoever professes it commits to live with a heart totally given to God, directing all their affective capacity toward Him and toward service of others.
English:en.En una sociedad donde el amor se mide po: In a society where love is measured by desire or usefulness, consecrated chastity reminds us that **true love does not possess, but gives itself away**. It is the love that does not demand, but welcomes; that does not use, but **frees**.
English:en.> “El amor casto muestra a los hombres y:
> “Chaste love shows modern men and women a path of healing from isolation, in a form of love that is free and liberating.”  
> — _Pope Francis_
English:en.El consagrado vive la castidad no como r: The consecrated person lives chastity not as repression, but as an **anticipation of heaven**, where “they will no longer marry, but will be like the angels of God” (Mt 22:30). In their heart beats the eternal love of the divine Spouse, a love that **embraces everyone without dividing**.
English:en.### 💧 El voto de pobreza: libre para ama: ### 💧 The vow of poverty: free to love
English:en.> “El consejo evangélico de pobreza, en: > “The evangelical counsel of poverty, in following Christ who, being rich, became poor for us, involves not only a life poor in fact and in spirit, but also a dependence and limitation in the use and disposition of goods according to the proper law of each institute.”
English:en.Vivir la pobreza evangélica no significa: Living evangelical poverty does not mean despising material goods, but **ordering them according to love**. The religious renounces possession, not because goods are bad, but because he wants **his only treasure to be God**.
English:en.En un mundo que idolatra el consumo y la: In a world that idolizes consumption and comfort, consecrated poverty reminds us that **“man does not live on bread alone” (Lk 4:4)**. It is a silent protest against selfishness and a proclamation of inner freedom.
English:en.Ser pobre por amor es poder decir: _“Mi: Being poor for love is being able to say: _“My wealth is Christ”_. It is living detached, in solidarity, and generously. It is not an emptiness, but a **full availability to serve** and to share.
English:en.> “La pobreza muestra cómo las cosas tie:
> “Poverty shows how things have value in the order of love, and rejects everything that can obscure its beauty: selfishness, greed, dependence.”  
> — _Pope Francis_
English:en.### 🔥 El voto de obediencia: escuchar y: ### 🔥 The vow of obedience: listening to and following Christ
English:en.> “El consejo evangélico de obediencia,: > “The evangelical counsel of obedience, assumed in a spirit of faith and love in following Christ obedient unto death, obliges one to submit the will to legitimate superiors when they command according to the constitutions of one's own institute.”
English:en.La obediencia es quizás el voto más exig: Obedience is perhaps the most demanding vow, because it touches the deepest part of the human person: his freedom. But it is also the one that **most transforms the soul into Christ**.
English:en.Jesús mismo fue “obediente hasta la muer: Jesus himself was “obedient unto death, even death on a cross” (Phil 2:8). The consecrated learns from Him to trust, to listen, to renounce himself out of love. To obey is not to submit blindly, but to **recognize the voice of God** in the mediation of the Church and of superiors.
English:en.> “La obediencia es signo para nuestra s:
> “Obedience is a sign for our society because it is based on listening to one another and then acting, even at the cost of renouncing one's own tastes and preferences.”  
> — _Pope Francis_
English:en.En una cultura que exalta la autonomía y: In a culture that exalts autonomy and the “I do what I want” attitude, the vow of obedience proclaims a forgotten truth: **true freedom is doing the will of God**.
English:en.Los votos no se viven en soledad. Cada c: Vows are not lived in solitude. Each consecrated man and woman belongs to a **community**, where faith, prayer, and mission are shared. It is a space where one learns to love concretely: in fraternal life, patience, forgiveness, service.
English:en.El religioso no busca sólo su santificac: The religious does not seek only his own sanctification, but **builds together with others a spiritual family**. The community thus becomes the visible face of the Kingdom of God, where all are brothers and sisters in Christ.
English:en.En un mundo sediento de autenticidad, lo: In a world thirsty for authenticity, religious men and women are **living signs of hope**, witnesses that it is worth giving everything for love.
English:en.**Seguir a Cristo pobre, casto y obedien: **Following Christ poor, chaste, and obedient does not impoverish life… it fills it with meaning.**

English:en.## **Elegir con quién compartir la vida*: ## **Choosing whom to share your life with**
English:en.**Elegir con quién compartir la vida** e:
**Choosing whom to share your life with** is one of the most important decisions a Christian can make.  
It is not only about **finding someone you like**, but about **discovering the person God is calling you to love and serve for life**.
English:en.**Amar con los ojos de Dios** significa: **To love with the eyes of God** means looking beyond emotion and impulse, and **learning to decide with the heart and the mind enlightened by faith.**
English:en.### **No te dejes cegar por los sentimie: ### **Do not let yourself be blinded by feelings**
English:en.El amor verdadero no es un _tsunami_ de:
True love is not a _tsunami_ of emotions that sweeps you away without thinking.  
In the early stages — attraction and falling in love — there is a strong emotional and hormonal charge that can cloud reason. It is normal, but you must let the wave subside in order to see clearly.
English:en.> **“Cuando te preguntas ‘¿me conviene?’:
"> **“When you ask yourself ‘is this right for me?’, you are on the right track.”**  
> Not because love is calculation, but because mature love knows how to discern.
English:en.Enamorarse no basta: **hay que decidir a:
Falling in love is not enough: **you must decide to love.**  
Or, as we often say: _you fall in love with the heart, but you choose with the head._
English:en.Hoy parece que las relaciones funcionan:
Today it seems relationships work like in TV series: two meet, have dinner, like each other… and everything rushes ahead.  
But love **does not grow by fits of impulse.**
English:en.La **sexualidad** está pensada como un *:
**Sexuality** is intended as a **language of conjugal love**, and when it is rushed, **it confuses.**  
The body promises what the soul has not yet decided to give.
English:en.> **“El sexo puede nublar el discernimie: "> **“Sex can cloud discernment: it makes you believe there is unity when it has not yet been built.”**
English:en.Muchos noviazgos se rompen porque **nunc:
Many engagements break up because **they never really got to know each other**, because they talked little and touched a lot.  
That is why the advice remains valid and wise:  
**talk a lot, pray together and touch little.**
English:en.El noviazgo **no es un “mini matrimonio”:
A relationship **is not a “mini marriage”**: it is a time to **discern whether that person is the one you want to share your life with.**  
It is not only about having a good time, but about **discovering if together you can grow in holiness.**
English:en.El **noviazgo cristiano** es una **escue:
**Christian courtship** is a **school of love**.  
It is not about possessing, but about **learning to give oneself, to respect, to understand.**
English:en.En él, uno aprende a pasar del **enamora: In it, one learns to move from **infatuation —which is feeling— to love —which is deciding—.**
English:en.Es el momento de conocerse a fondo:: It is the time to get to know each other deeply:
English:en.* Cómo vivís la fe: *   How do you live your faith
English:en.* Cómo reaccionáis ante el dolor o la: *   How do you react to pain or frustration
English:en.> **No basta con que la otra persona sea: > **It is not enough that the other person is good: you must see how you are together.**
English:en.* ¿Cómo actuamos cuando hay desacuerdo: *   How do we act when there are disagreements?
English:en.* ¿Sabemos pedir perdón y ceder?: *   Do we know how to apologize and give in?
English:en.* ¿Compartimos una misma fe y proyecto: *   Do we share the same faith and life project?
English:en.* ¿Nos ayudamos a ser mejores o nos de: *   Do we help each other become better or do we wear each other down?
English:en.* ¿Nos amamos con libertad, sin depend: *   Do we love each other freely, without emotional dependence?
English:en.El amor cristiano **no busca la perfecci: Christian love **does not seek the perfection of the other**, but **to walk together toward it.**
English:en.En el discernimiento de pareja hay que m:
In couple discernment you must look beyond the superficial.  
**A home is not built on beauty or charm, but on the soul.**  
Appearance passes; the heart and faith remain.
First, that he or she be **Christian, truly.**  
Not just baptized, but **a believer, a practicing person, someone who lives their faith** and wishes to walk with you toward God.
English:en.> Muchos matrimonios sufren porque se un:
> Many marriages suffer because they united without sharing the same faith, hoping the other would “change.”  
> **Love does not convert by itself: only grace and freedom do.**
English:en.También mira la **madurez**: cómo vive s: Also look at **maturity**: how their family lives, how they work, how they face difficulties, how they manage money, if they are responsible, faithful and honest.
English:en.No te fíes de los que **prometen mucho y:
Do not trust those who **promise a lot and live little.**  
Habits do not change by magic in marriage.
English:en.> **“Antes de viajar por tierra, ora; si:
> **“Before traveling by land, pray; if by sea, pray twice; and if you are going to marry, pray three times.”**  
> — _Russian proverb_
English:en.El matrimonio no se construye sobre una: Marriage is not built on a smile or a moment of tenderness, but on everything you are: **thoughts, dreams, wounds, hopes and faith.**
English:en.Casarse no es simplemente “quererse much:
Getting married is not simply “loving each other a lot.”  
It is **wanting to be spouses**, forming a **community of life open to children and to God.**
English:en.Por eso, el noviazgo debe ser un **camin: Therefore, courtship must be a **path of preparation**, a process in which one decides—with freedom and truth—whether that love can become a **sacrament.**
English:en.No te fíes de los flechazos ni de las pr:
Do not trust infatuations or haste.  
Nor appearance or attractiveness.  
Seek a **solid love, founded on faith, virtue and trust.**
English:en.**Elige con oración.** \nEscucha a quie:
**Choose with prayer.**  
Listen to those who love you: parents, priests, friends of faith.  
Ask for advice, but above all **ask God for light.**  
He knows your heart better than anyone.
English:en.**Amar con los ojos de Dios** es mirar a:
**To Love with God’s Eyes** is to look at the other as He looks at them: with **truth, tenderness, and demand.**  
It is **to desire the other’s good more than one’s own pleasure.**  
It is **to choose to love even when it is not felt**, and to trust that the feeling will return, purified and stronger.
English:en.> **“El amor humano es serio, grande y s: "> **“Human love is serious, great and holy.”**
English:en.Por eso hay que construirlo sobre cimien:
That is why it must be built on solid foundations:  
**prayer, chastity, sincerity, faith and the will to serve.**
English:en.**Elegir bien no es tener suerte:** \ne:

it is **knowing how to look with a heart in grace.**
English:en.Para llegar a ser sacerdote católico, un: To become a Catholic priest, a man must meet three basic requirements:
English:en.En una palabra: **intensa**, pero tambié:
In one word: **intense**, but also **full of life**.  
The demands of the priesthood are great, which is why formation is rigorous… but amid study and prayer there is **time to live together, laugh and share as brothers**.
English:en.Además de los estudios a nivel de maestr: In addition to graduate-level studies, seminarians:
English:en.* Rezán juntos al menos dos veces al d: *   Pray together at least twice a day.
English:en.* Realizan **prácticas pastorales** en: *   Carry out **pastoral internships** in local parishes.
English:en.Y entre todo eso, hay momentos para **el:
And among all that, there are times for **sports, gatherings, jokes in the refectory and long conversations among friends** that forge an authentic fraternity.  
Because the seminary not only forms priests: **it forms brothers who learn to live in community, with joy and with Christ at the center**.
English:en.Ser sacerdote **no es un trabajo**, sino:
Being a priest **is not a job**, but **a new identity**: becoming an _alter Christus_, another Christ.  
For this reason, the Church proposes a demanding formation in **four fundamental areas**:
English:en.1. **Formación humana:** cultivar una p: 1.  **Human formation:** cultivate a personality that is a **bridge to Christ** and that allows one to be an effective spokesperson for the Church.
English:en.2. **Formación espiritual:** desarrolla: 2.  **Spiritual formation:** develop a **deep and mature relationship with Christ** through prayer and a virtuous life.
English:en.3. **Formación intelectual:** conocer a: 3.  **Intellectual formation:** know thoroughly the **truths of the faith** and acquire the skills to teach them to others.
English:en.4. **Formación pastoral:** aprender a s: 4.  **Pastoral formation:** learning to be a true **shepherd of souls**, accompanying the faithful in their joys and sufferings.
English:en.El camino hacia el sacerdocio es una ver:
The path to the priesthood is a true adventure of grace: a **journey where the heart learns to listen, to serve and to love like Christ, the Good Shepherd**.  
In our seminary, each stage of formation has its own rhythm and beauty, helping each young man to grow in freedom, maturity and joyful self-giving.
English:en.Es el **primer año**, un tiempo para **c:
It is the **first year**, a time to **clarify and strengthen the priestly vocation**.  
It is a year of **prayer, community life and fraternity**, where each seminarian learns to let go of personal ideas about the vocation and open his heart to the **voice of God**.  
It focuses on **creating a life of prayer and brotherhood** that will sustain the entire formation journey. The year is lived in Alcalá de Henares, together with seminarians from Madrid and Alcalá, reinforcing discernment and fraternity.
English:en.En esta etapa contamos con **Nico y Alej: In this stage we have **Nico and Alejandro**, taking their first steps in faith and formation.
English:en.Normalmente dura **dos años** y tiene co:
It usually lasts **two years** and aims to **verify and strengthen the vocational choice** through discipleship.  
Here the seminarian **lives the interior life through following Jesus**, grows in virtues, dedicates himself to the **study of Philosophy** and actively participates in **social and charitable activities**.
English:en.En esta etapa tenemos a **Álvaro y Carlo: In this stage we have **Álvaro and Carlos**, deepening their spiritual and pastoral life.
English:en.Normalmente dura **tres años** y se dedi:
It usually lasts **three years** and is devoted to the **assimilation and identification with the being and ministry of the diocesan priest**.  
The seminarian is configured to Christ, the Good Shepherd, integrating **all aspects of his personality in the choice of the presbyterate**.  
He deepens in prayer, personal communion with God, the **study of Theology** and on weekends he dedicates himself to **pastoral work in the parish** to which he is assigned.
English:en.En esta etapa contamos con **Andrés,** e: In this stage we have **Andrés,** in his third year of the seminary:
English:en.Y **Andoni y Miguel**, en sexto curso, c: And **Andoni and Miguel**, in the sixth year, growing in experience and pastoral dedication.
English:en.Es **el año de inserción pastoral** y de:
It is **the year of pastoral insertion** and of final preparation for the presbyterate.  
It is the **synthesis of the formation journey**, where usually the **orders of the diaconate** are received and, at the end, the **priesthood**.  
It is about **living the total giving of life and service to all**, consolidating everything learned in the previous stages.

English:en.A pesar de esta vocación universal, **mu: Despite this universal vocation, **many baptized people have not yet become fully aware of their belonging to the Church**. Many consider themselves Catholic, but do not experience the Church as **a home that transforms their life and surroundings**. This creates situations where Christian values are seen as something “optional” or cultural, rather than being **the foundation of their identity**.
English:en.* La vida profesional, política, econó: *   Professional, political, economic, scientific, artistic and media life **is not always guided by evangelical criteria**.
English:en.* Existe una **incoherencia entre la f: *   There is an **incoherence between the professed faith and real commitment** in everyday life.

English:en.* Deficiencias en la **formación integ: *   Deficiencies in **integral formation**, which prevent responding effectively to the current challenges of society.
English:en.Estos factores hacen necesario un **rede: These factors make a **profound rediscovery of the lay vocation** necessary. Being Christian is not just performing religious practices: **it is having a vocation**, and being lay means **ordering all social life from within**, from the depths of present reality, with the light of the Gospel.
English:en.El **Concilio Vaticano II** restableció: The **Second Vatican Council** restored the **permanent diaconate** (LG 29) and defined it as _“a proper and permanent degree within the hierarchy”_. It may be conferred on **married men** who receive the **sacrament of orders** in its **third degree**.
English:en.Los diáconos son **fortalecidos por la i: Deacons are **strengthened by the imposition of hands** that comes from the Apostles and are more closely united to the **service of the altar**, fulfilling their ministry with the **grace of the diaconate** (AG 16).
English:en.El diácono está llamado a vivir la _diak: The deacon is called to live the _diakonía_ — the **service** — that characterizes his vocation. His mission is threefold: **to serve the Word, the Liturgy and Charity**.
English:en.* Administrar los **sacramentos del Ba:
*   Administering the **sacraments of Baptism and Matrimony**.
*   **Assisting the priest** in the Eucharist, **proclaiming the Gospel** and **distributing Communion**, both in the church and to the sick.
*   **Preaching**, **giving catechesis** and **presiding at funerals**.
*   **Administering parishes** and coordinating works of charity.
English:en.El diácono no sustituye al sacerdote ni: The deacon does not replace the priest or the layperson, but has **a proper identity and mission**, within the single service to the People of God.
English:en.El diaconado se apoya en el **Nuevo Test: The diaconate is supported by the **New Testament** and expresses Christ's command about service:
English:en.> “No he venido a que me sirvan, sino a: "> “I have not come to be served, but to serve” (cf. Lk 22:27).
English:en.Jesús se presenta como el **primer diáco: Jesus presents himself as the **first deacon**, the servant par excellence.
English:en.En los **Hechos de los Apóstoles**, los: In the **Acts of the Apostles**, the Twelve choose **seven men of good repute**, full of the Holy Spirit, to serve the tables and help those in need (Acts 6:1-6). Among them are notable **Stephen**, the first martyr, and **Philip**, called _“the evangelist”_ (Acts 21:8).
English:en.Desde los primeros siglos, el diaconado: Since the early centuries, the diaconate closely accompanied the bishop and had great importance in ecclesial life. Deacon **Saint Lawrence**, patron and example, was administrator and almoner of the Church of Rome, a model of dedication and fidelity.
English:en.El **Concilio Vaticano II** recuperó el: The **Second Vatican Council** restored the diaconate as a stable ministry, with **its own identity and mission**, opening a new stage in the life of the Church.
English:en.El diaconado permanente sigue creciendo: The permanent diaconate continues to grow as a **response of the Holy Spirit** to the current needs of the Church. English:en.### Cuando toca soltar: ### When it is time to let go
English:en.A veces, el amor también se purifica en:
Sometimes, love is also purified in **renunciation**. There are relationships that are not meant to continue, and discerning this with sincerity and prayer is also an act of love.  
Breaking up does not always mean failing: it can be the most honest and courageous way to love. God does not bless every relationship, but the one that leads us to holiness and to true self-giving.
English:en.**Soltar con paz** es reconocer que el o: **Letting go with peace** is recognizing that the other belongs to God before they belong to us, and that happiness is not measured by keeping, but by loving in freedom.
English:en.> “Amar es querer el bien del otro, aunq: "> “To love is to will the good of the other, even if that good does not include me.”
English:en.Después de una ruptura, pueden quedar he:
After a breakup, wounds, feelings of guilt or emptiness may remain. But the heart is not made to stay broken: **God can heal** what seemed lost.  
It is a time of silence, prayer and accompaniment. Of letting grace repair what human love could not.
English:en.Los sacramentos, la dirección espiritual: The sacraments, spiritual direction and friendship are medicine. The Eucharist sustains, confession frees, prayer consoles. It is not only about “turning the page”, but about **letting God write a new one**.
English:en.Las pruebas del amor no son un obstáculo: The trials of love are not an obstacle, but a purification. Mature love is born from pain embraced with faith. When it gives itself, forgives and learns, the heart expands and loves better.
English:en.Por eso, incluso las rupturas pueden ser: Therefore, even breakups can be part of the vocational path: they help to get to know oneself, to purify desires and to prepare to love like Christ, with truth and without fear.
English:en.* No tengas miedo de pedir ayuda: habl: *   Do not be afraid to ask for help: talking with a priest or a spiritual companion can clarify a lot.
English:en.* No idealices ni te encierres: el nov: *   Do not idealize or lock yourself away: Christian courtship is a path of freedom, not of dependence.
English:en.* No apagues la esperanza: si Dios ha: *   Do not extinguish hope: if God has permitted a wound, it is because He wants to bring forth a greater love from it.
English:en.La vocación es el compromiso profundo de: Vocation is the deep commitment to follow God's call. It requires effort and care to truly understand that call. This process of discovering God's will is known as **vocational discernment**.
English:en.El discernimiento adecuado implica vario: Proper discernment involves several key elements:
English:en.* **Profundo autoconocimiento:** compr: *   **Deep self-knowledge:** understanding your personality, your strengths and weaknesses, your inclinations, your spirituality, your mental capacities and even your physical health.
English:en.* **Un conocimiento sólido y un amor s: *   **A solid knowledge of and a sincere love for our Catholic faith.**
English:en.* **Familiaridad con las diferentes vo: *   **Familiarity with the different vocations**, what they entail and the way of life they shape in those who embrace them.
English:en.Naturalmente, este proceso no sucede de: Naturally, this process does not happen overnight. Vocational discernment is a **journey** that can take months or even years. It requires study, prayer and, above all, patience.
English:en.* El discernimiento **no es algo que s: *   Discernment **is not something that can be done alone**. The best way to discern is with the guidance of the Church, ideally accompanied by a priest or a trusted spiritual director who helps you discover where God may be calling you.
English:en.* Si buscas orientación —ya sea que te: *   If you seek guidance —whether you have simple questions or need deeper accompaniment—, **we are here to help you!**

English:en.### El noviazgo como vocación y camino d: ### Courtship as a vocation and a path of giving
English:en.**El noviazgo no es un paréntesis en la:
**Courtship is not a parenthesis in Christian life, but a true call to love as Christ.**  
Just as marriage is a vocation to unconditional giving, courtship is a time of discernment and maturation in love. It is the stage where two people get to know each other, discover one another and prepare to decide if they want to give themselves to each other forever.
English:en.### Un tiempo de discernimiento y gracia: ### A time of discernment and grace
English:en.Cada cristiano está llamado a la santida: Every Christian is called to holiness —including those who are engaged—. This time is not a pause, but an opportunity to grow in faith and virtue. Living courtship with God at the center means letting Him give meaning to the relationship: illuminating affections, purifying intentions and making love fruitful.
English:en.Cuando un amor te acerca más a Dios y te: When a love draws you closer to God and helps you love others better, there is a Christian courtship. The more engaged couples love each other, the more capable they are of loving God, and vice versa.
> “The heart was created to love. Let us therefore put Christ into all our loves.”
English:en.Amar no es solo sentir, sino aprender a: To love is not only to feel, but to learn to give of oneself. Courtship is a school of love where virtues are forged: respect, patience, generosity and fidelity. Small gestures —listening, yielding, waiting— prepare for a love that endures.
English:en.También es un tiempo para **formarse y c: It is also a time to **form and grow together**. Reading, dialoguing, sharing concerns about faith and marriage helps to build on rock. It is important to be accompanied, seek counsel and learn from those who have already walked this path.
English:en.Un amor auténtico cuida y respeta. La ca: Authentic love cares for and respects. Chastity is not a denial of love, but its protection. It teaches how to love without using, to wait to give oneself fully, to discover the beauty of the beloved person as a gift. Christian courtship is not measured by the intensity of desire, but by the depth of respect and the truth of commitment.
English:en.> Amar es ayudar al otro a ser santo, no: > To love is to help the other become holy, not to be an obstacle on their way to God.
English:en.El noviazgo también es tiempo de **amist: Courtship is also a time of friendship, laughter and shared life. It is not about isolating yourselves in the relationship, but about opening up together to the world: serving, doing apostolate, living the faith with joy. A Christian couple not only loves each other: they are a witness to God's love in the midst of the world.
English:en.Los novios que rezan juntos, que van a M: Couples who pray together, who go to Mass, who confess, who put God at the center, experience that their love becomes stronger and freer. In the sacraments one finds the grace to forgive one another, understand one another and grow in communion.
English:en.El noviazgo es, en definitiva, **una voc: Courtship is, ultimately, a vocation to true love, an invitation to learn to love as Christ loves his Church: with patience, with tenderness and with self-giving.
English:en.El papel de la familia y la comunidad: The role of the family and the community
English:en.### **El primer hogar de la vocación: la: ### The first home of the vocation: the family
English:en.Toda vocación comienza en casa. No en un:
Every vocation begins at home. Not in a seminary, nor in a convent, but in the warmth of a family that prays, loves and serves.  
There one learns to say “yes”, to look beyond oneself, to discover that life becomes great when it is given away.
English:en.* La familia es el **primer seminario: *   The family is the first seminary of the heart.
English:en.* Donde se enseña a **hablar con Dios: *   Where one is taught to speak with God naturally.
English:en.* Donde se aprende que la fe **no es t: *   Where one learns that faith is not theory, but shared life.
English:en.### **La comunidad: cuna donde crece la: ### The community: cradle where the call grows
English:en.Nadie discierne solo. \nLa **comunidad:
No one discerns alone.  
The parish community, the group, the movement, are places where faith becomes a living experience.  
There one discovers one’s gifts, shares concerns and finds concrete models of self-giving.
English:en.👉 La comunidad no sustituye la voz de Di:
👉 The community does not replace the voice of God, but it helps to recognize it.  
👉 It accompanies, encourages, supports… and prays.
English:en.> _Una comunidad que reza por las vocaci: "> _A community that prays for vocations makes them be born._
English:en.Necesitamos familias y comunidades que *:
We need families and communities that live their own vocation with joy, knowing that this already is a testimony.  
When a married couple lives united, when a priest serves with passion, when a religious sister smiles with faith, they are preaching with their life.
English:en.La vocación no es un tema del pasado ni:
Vocation is not a topic of the past nor only for “others”.  
It is the great adventure of every Christian: discovering how God wants to love the world through you.
English:en.🌾 **Padres, catequistas, sacerdotes, ami:
🌾 Parents, catechists, priests, friends…  
Let us speak of vocation naturally.  
Let us look at our young people with eyes of faith:
English:en.> “Este chico sería un buen sacerdote.”:
"> “That boy would make a good priest.”  
> “That girl has a big heart for serving.”
English:en.Y no solo lo pensemos: **recemos por ell:
And not only think it: let us pray for them.  
Every prayer is a seed in God's field.
English:en.Vive tu familia como Iglesia: ama, entre: Live your family as Church: love, give of yourselves and be a beacon of God's love in the world.
English:en.Cristo quiso nacer y crecer en la Sagrad: Christ wanted to be born and grow in the Holy Family of Joseph and Mary. From its origins, the family has been the first nucleus of Christian life, where faith is taught, lived and transmitted. Every believing home is a domestic Church, a place where the love of God is first preached through mutual self-giving and daily example.
English:en.Los padres son los **primeros predicador:
Parents are the first preachers of the faith. With their words and above all with their example, they teach their children to live in God.  
They foster vocations and help discover the personal call of each family member. Holiness is learned at home, in patience, forgiveness, work and daily prayer.
English:en.**Imagen sugerida:** Padres leyendo la B: **Suggested image:** Parents reading the Bible to their children, showing closeness and unity.
English:en.#### **Comunidad de fe, esperanza y cari: #### Community of faith, hope and charity
English:en.La familia cristiana es **una comunión d:
The Christian family is a communion of persons, reflecting the communion that exists in God between Father, Son and Holy Spirit.  
Through prayer, the sacraments and daily life, members exercise the baptismal priesthood, offering their lives as a sign of love and self-giving. Here one learns to be generous, patient and to love without reserves.
English:en.**Imagen sugerida:** Familia en oración: **Suggested image:** Family in joint prayer, in an attitude of recollection.
English:en.Como Dios crea y educa, la familia parti: As God creates and educates, the family participates in his work: to procreate, educate and form in love. Every home is an image of God, responsible for transmitting life, love and hope. The family’s mission begins by first preaching the love of God among its members, in daily self-giving and mutual care.
English:en.**Imagen sugerida:** Familia abrazada en: **Suggested image:** Family embracing in a natural landscape, reflecting love and creation.
English:en.#### Misión que ilumina el mundo: #### A mission that illuminates the world
English:en.Vivir la fe en familia no es solo cuidar: Living the faith in the family is not only caring for one’s own home, it is being a beacon for others. The everyday acts of love and service teach children and show those around us that the Christian life is true and beautiful. The family evangelizes by its example, its commitment and its self-giving.
English:en.**Imagen sugerida:** Familia participand: **Suggested image:** Family participating in parish activities or community service.
Family prayer unites and strengthens. Reading the Word of God, praying together and putting God at the center of daily life makes a difference in decisions, behaviors and emotional bonds.  
If the home revolves only around the worldly, the sacred dimension of life is lost. A family that prays remains united and transmits faith.
English:en.**Imagen sugerida:** Familia rezando ant: **Suggested image:** Family praying before a meal or at a commonplace moment of union.
English:en.La familia cristiana es **una Iglesia vi: The Christian family is a living Church present in the world, a reflection of God's love. Each member has the dignity and the responsibility to preach first with life and self-giving to the other. The home not only lives the faith, it radiates it; it forms, accompanies and evangelizes. Being a Christian family is a call to love without limits, to overcome selfishness and to live total self-giving, as God loves us.
English:en.**Imagen sugerida al final:** Collage de: **Suggested final image:** Collage of Christian families in prayer, celebrations and service, showing unity and diversity.
English:en.1. ¿Qué hace un sacerdote? \n El pr:
1.  What does a priest do?  
    The purpose of a priest is to lead people to Jesus and to bring Jesus to the people. He does this mainly by preaching the Word and offering the Sacrifice of the Mass.
English:en.Su vida diaria consiste en administrar l: His daily life consists in administering the sacraments —Baptism, Confirmation, Eucharist, Penance and Reconciliation, Anointing of the Sick and Matrimony (Holy Orders is administered by the bishop)— and in attending to the spiritual and human needs of his community.
English:en.2. ¿Qué es exactamente una “vocación”?:
2.  What exactly is a “vocation”?  
    A vocation is a call from God to do something specific for Him and for his Kingdom. The primary vocation of every person is to be holy: to love and serve God, obey his commandments and cooperate with Christ in the work of redemption by loving and serving others.
English:en.Pero todos somos llamados también a una: But we are all also called to a secondary vocation, a “state of life” in which we must be holy.
English:en.3. ¿Cuáles son esas “vocaciones secunda:
3.  What are those “secondary vocations” to which I might be called?  
    Many people are called to marriage, but it is a mistake to assume automatically that this is your vocation. You may also be called to the priesthood, to religious life as a brother or sister, or to the diaconate.
English:en.Finalmente, algunos siguen a Cristo en e: Finally, some follow Christ in the state of celibate life. Remember: it is normal to desire marriage and family. That desire does not exclude that you may have a priestly vocation.
English:en.4. ¿Cómo puedo saber a qué me llama Dio:
4.  How can I know what God is calling me to?  
    You should pray every day asking God to reveal His plan to you. Do not ask yourself: “What do I want to do when I grow up?”, but: “Jesus, what do You want me to do?”. And listen for the answer!
English:en.El lugar principal donde Dios habla es e: The primary place where God speaks is the heart. Listen with your heart. Also, the discernment of a priestly vocation is always done within the Church. The local bishop, assisted by the vocational office and the seminary, is the one who ultimately confirms the call.
English:en.5. ¿Puedo ser feliz si no sigo el plan:
5.  Can I be happy if I do not follow the plan God has for me?  
    If you do not follow the vocation for which you were created, you can attain some happiness in this life and still be saved, but you will never be as fully happy as if you followed your true vocation.
English:en.Por eso es tan importante discernir corr: That is why it is so important to discern correctly. Of course every vocation has trials and difficulties, but there is also great joy in giving your life for Jesus.
English:en.6. ¿Son felices la mayoría de los sacer:
6.  Are most priests happy in their vocation?  
    Most priests are very happy! Priestly life is deeply rewarding, both in this life and in the life to come.
English:en.Los medios de comunicación a veces dan u: The media sometimes give a distorted image of priests, presenting them as frustrated or unhappy, or reducing them to the scandals of a few. That simply is not true.
English:en.7. ¿Por qué los sacerdotes no pueden ca:
7.  Why can’t priests marry? Isn’t that very difficult?  
    Priests of the Roman Rite do not marry in order to dedicate themselves completely to Jesus and to His people. They beget “spiritual children” by bringing many souls to Christ and helping them grow in holiness.
English:en.El celibato es un signo poderoso para el: Celibacy is a powerful sign to the world that only Jesus can give us the happiness we all long for. Renouncing marriage and family shows that Christ is real and worthy of giving one’s life for Him.
English:en.Toda vocación exige sacrificios, pero ha: Every vocation demands sacrifices, but there is great joy in sacrificing for love. As one priest said: “It is true that no one will call me ‘dad,’ but thousands call me ‘father’.”
English:en.8. ¿Alguna vez se permitirá que los sac:
8.  Will priests ever be allowed to marry?  
    Celibacy will always exist in the Church because it is not only a law but a charism, a spiritual gift and a source of fruitfulness. Jesus was celibate. Saint Paul was too.
English:en.El celibato ayuda al sacerdote a unirse: Celibacy helps the priest to unite more intimately with Christ and to be a sign of the Kingdom of God. Although there are some married priests in the Catholic Church, they are exceptional cases.
English:en.Si alguna vez el Espíritu Santo quisiera: If the Holy Spirit ever wanted a change, He would effect it through the Pope and the bishops. But it would be a grave mistake to enter the seminary “hoping” that this will happen.
English:en.9. ¿Habría más sacerdotes si pudieran c:
9.  Would there be more priests if they could marry?  
    Maybe, but the question is whether that would be best for the Church. Celibacy for the sake of the Kingdom is a powerful testimony that Jesus is real and worthy of total self-giving.
English:en.Además, las vocaciones sacerdotales han: Moreover, priestly vocations have grown enormously in recent decades in Africa, Asia and Latin America, while they have declined in Europe and the United States. The problem is not celibacy, but deeper cultural and social factors.
English:en.10. ¿Estaré solo si me hago sacerdote?:
10.  Will I be lonely if I become a priest?  
    Loneliness is part of every vocation, but priests are rarely alone: they accompany people at the most important moments of their lives —birth, sacraments, marriage, death— and live surrounded by their community.
English:en.Cuando llega la soledad, Jesús llena ese: When loneliness comes, Jesus fills that emptiness, as He does in every vocation.
English:en.11. ¿Los sacerdotes reciben salario? \:
11.  Do priests receive a salary?  
    Yes, although they lead a simple life. They receive what is necessary to cover their expenses, maintain a vehicle, rest and carry out normal activities. In addition, the parish provides their lodging and food, so their expenses are minimal.
English:en.12. ¿Pueden divertirse los sacerdotes?:
12.  Can priests have fun?  
    Of course. Priests can practice sports, watch movies, read, travel, go to the theater, fish, play soccer or golf, as long as it is consistent with Christian life.
English:en.13. Si me atrae el sacerdocio, ¿signifi:
13.  If I am attracted to the priesthood, does that mean I have a vocation?  
    Possibly, but not necessarily. It is important to pray, attend Mass, live as a Christian and talk with a priest or the vocational director. They can help you discern clearly.
English:en.14. No soy muy “santo”. ¿Aun así puedo:
14.  I am not very “holy”. Can I still be a priest?  
    Yes. Holiness is a lifelong journey. God forms His priests little by little. Use the sacrament of Confession, pray daily and you will see how Christ transforms you.
English:en.15. ¿Es fácil llegar a ser sacerdote?:
15.  Is it easy to become a priest?  
    No. Serious formation is required: four years of college (including philosophy) and another four in the seminary to obtain the master’s in theology. But do not be discouraged: the seminary is a wonderful experience and God gives the necessary grace.
English:en.16. ¿Es necesaria tanta educación? \n:
16.  Is so much education necessary?  
    Yes. The priest must be well formed in the humanities, theology and spiritual life to serve with wisdom and be respected by the faithful. Every soul is precious and deserves a prepared pastor.
English:en.17. ¿Qué cualidades busca la Iglesia en:
17.  What qualities does the Church look for in a candidate?  
    He must be a practicing Catholic, who prays every day, lives the commandments, serves others, enjoys good physical, mental and emotional health, and has average or above-average intelligence. Above all, he must be open to the will of God.
English:en.18. Si entro al seminario “para probar”:
18.  If I enter the seminary “to try it out”, am I already committed for life?  
    No. The seminary is precisely the place to discern. Many men enter, test it for a while and then choose another path. And even so, they leave strengthened in their faith.
English:en.19. ¿Es interesante la vida del sacerdo:
19.  Is the life of a priest interesting?  
    Very much! Each day is different. There are challenges, but also a deep joy. At the end of the day, the priest can say: “Lord, today I have given myself for You”. There is no fuller way to live.

English:en.## **¿Cómo saber si Dios me llama? — Ven: ## How to know if God is calling me? — Overcoming fear
English:en.Quizá alguna vez haya pasado por tu ment: Perhaps the idea of the priesthood has at times crossed your mind, but fear drives it away:
English:en.* Miedo al compromiso\n* Miedo al ce:
*   Fear of commitment
*   Fear of celibacy
*   Fear of not being worthy
English:en.Estos temores son muy comunes, incluso e: These fears are very common, even among those already in the seminary. But literally thousands of men have had the same doubts and yet became holy and devoted priests.
English:en.La primera verdad que debes recordar es: The first truth you must remember is that God does not speak through fear. Fear is a weapon of the Enemy to turn you away from God’s will; it is like the bite of an animal that paralyses its prey so it cannot move.
English:en.Un hombre dominado por el miedo tendrá d: A man dominated by fear will have difficulty advancing toward God’s will.
English:en.Entonces, ¿cómo superar el miedo? Aquí t: So, how to overcome fear? Here are five ideas:
English:en.Puedes tener preocupaciones legítimas so: You may have legitimate concerns about celibacy or preaching, but that is not the same as being afraid. Instead of letting fear dominate you, look at the demands of the priesthood objectively. It is true that a priest needs self-control, emotional maturity and the ability to speak in public. These and other areas require serious personal examination.
English:en.Sí, descubrirás cosas que debes mejorar,: Yes, you will discover things you must improve, but make your discernment with a calm mind, not with a frightened heart.
English:en.Recuerda que cuando Jesús llamó a Pedro: Remember that when Jesus called Peter (Lk 5:1-11), the first Pope said to him:
English:en.> “Apártate de mí, Señor, que soy un pec: > “Go away from me, Lord; I am a sinful man.”
English:en.Y Jesús le aseguró que no debía tener mi: And Jesus assured him that he should not be afraid to follow him. Likewise, Jesus knows your weaknesses and difficulties. If you trust in Him and “cast the nets into the deep,” everything will turn out well.
English:en.### **2) Reflexiona sobre el amor de Dio: ### **2) Reflect on the love of God.**
English:en.El P. Brett Brannen, en su libro _Salvar: Fr. Brett Brannen, in his book _Saving a Thousand Souls_, recommends this meditation when a man feels afraid:
English:en.> “Dios es infinito en poder y me ama in: > “God is infinite in power and loves me infinitely. No one can snatch me out of his hand. God will never send me where his grace cannot sustain me. If he asks something difficult of me, like becoming a priest, he will give me the grace to do it. I will not fail, because He is with me. I will be happy because I do his will. Even if I do not have all the necessary qualities, God will help me develop them. In his will is my peace.”
English:en.### **3) Confía tus miedos a la Virgen M: ### **3) Entrust your fears to the Virgin Mary.**
English:en.Recuerda que, después de que el ángel le: Remember that after the angel told her “do not be afraid,” Mary readily accepted God’s will:
English:en.> “He aquí la esclava del Señor; hágase: > “Behold the servant of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word.”
English:en.Entrégale tus temores a su intercesión:: Give your fears to her intercession: she will calm your heart and help you discover the will of her Son.
English:en.### **4) Recuerda para qué es el seminar: ### **4) Remember what the seminary is for.**
English:en.Desde un punto de vista práctico, es con: From a practical point of view, it is consoling to know that, if God calls you to the priesthood, ordination is still far off. The seminary is a time of intense formation to confront doubts, grow in holiness and prepare for fruitful ministry. **No man enters the seminary already ready to be a priest.**
English:en.### **5) Busca consuelo en la Palabra de: ### **5) Find consolation in the Word of God.**
English:en.Si tienes miedo al sacerdocio, no estás: If you are afraid of the priesthood, you are not alone. Prophets and apostles also felt fear when they were called. Read the following biblical passages to see how God encouraged them:

English:en.Permanece fiel a la oración diaria, conf: Remain faithful to daily prayer, trust in God and your heart will be at peace, whatever your vocation may be.

English:en.La misión de la Iglesia no es sólo de lo: The mission of the Church is not only for priests. Every baptized faithful has a unique place in the history of salvation.
